So well directed. But also so flawed. I’ll always be a fan of Spike Lee but he’s newer work really lacks the bite of his earlier work. Do the Right Thing and Malcolm X clear this. Some amazing sequences and humor but the thin line between fiction and reality and the cop-ness of it all really drags it down. The real life story is certainly compelling but the story decides to fictionalize some incredibly important aspects such as Flip’s identity, Ron’s personal philosophy, and Patrice. Patrice is the most frustrating part of all of this because she is an incredibly compelling character and her and Ron’s conversation about Blackxploitation films on the bridge is arguably one of the best scenes (shout out Shaft). If you’re going to tell a “true” story, don’t let the fictional stuff become more compelling than the real life story. This is clearly meant to be a response to modern politics and an analysis of the growth of political racism in the United States, which is incredibly compelling but it loses all credibility when the whole police department of an incredibly right wing town are all relatively supportive of the black guy (expect for the one guy but the writers clearly wanted a scapegoat). It’s just so frustrating because this is entertaining and well done but the political messaging of it is all over the place.

John David Washington is flexing his muscles here, but this is just as much Spike Lee showing off. That restless, slightly disorienting visual style somehow feels like the only way this story could've been told. The more ridiculous the narrative becomes, the more natural his direction feels. Also realised how musically driven his films are. I still can't quite work out how this became his biggest, though. Do the Right Thing deserves to be just as ubiquitous. Really wasn't prepared for that final sequence either. Lee has a knack for pulling the rug out from under you just when you think you've settled into his rhythm. If anything, it's only made me more excited to finally watch Malcolm X later this year.

Apesar de ter se tornado algo super politizado no final, eu ainda sim adorei o filme. Infiltrados na Klan é literalmente uma denúncia a "seitas" que ainda acontecem por pessoas da elite nos EUA, e é aquele tipo de filme que contém várias verdades "discretas", e situações que realmente ocorreram na vida real. Um ponto negativo é que o filme foi lançado justo em época de eleição, e eu senti que o criador tentou fazer da KKK uma ligação ao Trump, oque não faz sentido já que a KKK existe a mais de 50 anos. E pela história do policial ser realmente verídica, essa "ficção" faz toda a luta e investigação do policial parecer mentira. Mas entre toda via, este filme é importantíssimo, e conta uma história real da sociedade. E além disso, todo o preconceito e racismo que rola ao decorrer do filme, é só um espelho do que realmente acontece nesse confederado ridículo.

A really good movie that I’d wanted to see for a long time. The performances are great, especially John David Washington and Adam Driver. One of the best parts of the movie is the unbelievable score. It’s incredible and works so well throughout. The undercover premise is fascinating, and the movie is genuinely funny while still dealing with a very serious topic. The shifts in tone actually work really well rather than feeling uneven. It also taught me quite a lot about the KKK, and the movie itself is very well made and shot. The final act is really strong, and the pacing throughout is excellent and I really love that ending. Overall, a fun, engaging and interesting movie with great performances, a fantastic score and a lot of strong elements. 8.4/10

30 for 30: 2018 BlacKKKlansman✊🏿👻 This Spike Lee joint tells the story of two cops, one white and one black, that launch an operation to go undercover within the KKK. What comes out is a haunting yet still very relevant look at an America built on a racism. While I don’t think anything can ever top Do the Right Thing, I’m always seated for whatever this director puts out. I think what made that film an all timer for me is it asks a lot of questions about what is the “Right Thing”, particularly when it comes to inequality. I think this movie kind of builds on that theme, but amplifies it to a much higher degree with greater consequences. A fitting thing for when this movie came out that is still the same today. Politics are much more polarizing today. But, I also think Lee is much more unapologetic to excuses for racism than even his early films. The last 5 minutes of this lays it out clear. There are still limits to changing the system from within and hate has been on the rise again. Movie MVP: Going to go with Spike here. The director adds such a cool groove to this film that makes it feel both like a film in the 1970s, when it takes place, and in the late 2010s. It is bleak subject matter for sure, especially when the director uses real world examples of racial injustice and racism. Also really liked how the director challenged different forms of hate and how it should be tackled. Adam Driver’s character is just one example of this. He may not be visibly a target of racism, yet he is Jewish and would be the target of the same hate groups. There’s an interesting question in here of “well, why aren’t you doing more?” when fighting injustice that affects everyone. I think Spike does a good job of showing there are the good things that can come from working together to tackle such subjects. Favourite quotes: “You know the way to sell hate? Affirmative action, immigration, crime, tax reform, he says no one wants to be called a bigot anymore because Archie Bunker made that too uncool. So, the idea is under all these issues…everyday Americans can accept it. Support it. Until eventually, one day he gets somebody in the White House that embodies it.” “Sheeeeeeee-it!”

A cureldade do ser humano se torna ainda maior quando há mais ser humanos que partilham da mesma crueldade. É triste ver um filme desse, principalmente com esse final; um final que demonstra a realidade mais crua e triste: a luta ainda persiste. Mesmo com provas, pessoas confessando, pessoas manifestando estas ideias em discursos, atos e ideologias, ainda há quem diga diga estes movimentos não são nocivos. A realidade dói, mas, se não a vermos, ninguem verá. O filme é bem construído, todos personagens são bons, apesar que tinham potenciais para serem melhores. A crítica sutil que demonstra a impossibilidade de sermos diferentes é cômica e certeira. Durante todo filme você fica curioso para entender como vai se findar aquela situação, se vai resolver ou não e qual lado vai ganhar esta guerra. Uma luta de tamanha proporção nunca se findaria com um pequeno movimento e, por esse motivo, que ela perdura até os dias de hoje.
